ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, the general partner, and legal representatives against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and Luxembourg domestic alert lists. Screening must be completed before acceptance of the incorporation file and repeated at least quarterly and upon any trigger event. PEP determination follows FATF Recommendations 12 and 22; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, high-risk third countries, and material discrepancies in UBO declarations. Any suspicious activity must be reported to the Cellule de Renseignements Financiers (CRF) under Article 5 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004. CDD records must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-Desk via lbr.lu, with supporting statutory e-filing through Guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names are recorded in the RCS in Latin script. The name may be in French, German, English, or another Latin-script language, but non-Latin characters must be transliterated into Latin script. The registered name of the SCSp must contain the mandatory suffix 'SCSp' or 'societe en commandite speciale'. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not imply any public authority, regulated financial activity, or protected statutory designation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: OPCVM / SICAV / SICAF / Fonds / Fund / Investment Fund
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Names are cleared through a 'certificat de non-confusion' (negative certificate) issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers. The certificate remains valid for 90 days from issue. No extension of a certificate is allowed; if the original certificate lapses, a new request may be filed, subject to priority of intervening third-party registrations. If the RCS rejects the name, counsel must obtain a written refusal or justification. A corrected application may be refiled without delay. If rejection persists, the applicant may commence administrative review before the LBR/RCS and, if necessary, challenge the refusal before the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg in summary proceedings within 15 days of notification. Local counsel is mandatory for the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to mandatory compliance with the Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation. An SCSp must use a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent for virtual-office arrangements. The registered office must be a physical Luxembourg address where legal documents can be validly served and official records are kept. A purely virtual mailbox without a licensed agent is not acceptable. For the stated low-risk digital publishing and health-data application activity, a licensed domiciliation structure is sufficient; higher-risk regulated activities would require additional physical substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5-10% likelihood within the first 24 months for a passive SCSp using a licensed domiciliation agent. The risk rises to approximately 25% if the entity files payroll, VAT, or public-tender documentation, and to approximately 35% if the UBO filing contains discrepancies, sanctions hits, or inconsistent commercial substance indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 902-1 to 902-15 (SCSp provisions introduced by the Law of 11 February 2013); Law of 23 July 2016 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL); amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions (business establishment permit); GDPR and Luxembourg Law of 1 August 2018 on data protection.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constituent deed / Articles of Association of the SCSp (Acte constitutif / Statuts), filed with the RCSL and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; zero-capital formation is permitted. No escrow account or bank capital attestation is required by Luxembourg law. Partnership capital, profit-sharing and contribution terms (cash, in-kind or industry) are contractually defined in the partnership agreement; legal personality and third-party opposability arise only upon RCSL registration and RESA publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the initial subscriptions of partnership interests in the SCSp, per the Subscription Schedule, are hereby accepted, and the registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed Manager (gérant) with full authority to represent the SCSp, open bank accounts, accept the digital health app business scope, and bind the partnership. RESOLVED that the Manager is authorized to register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), publish in the RESA, obtain the business establishment permit for ISIC 6201, register for VAT, and complete CNPD data-protection filings, taking all ancillary steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search, Reservation and Registered Office Vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCSL online name-check module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Launch the compulsory pre-incorporation name search on the LBR public platform to ensure the proposed SCSp name is not misleading and does not create confusion with existing registrations. Confirm that the name includes or is accompanied by the legal form designation 'SCSp' on all corporate documents. Obtain the landlord's written consent to the Luxembourg registered office and certify that the address is suitable for statutory service of process before engaging the notary.
required_dossiers: Name availability search confirmation
Draft articles with SCSp designation
Landlord consent / lease undertaking for registered office
Identity details of the general partner and initial limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or disputed, select and reserve two alternative names, re-file the LBR search, and amend the draft deed before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Constituent Partnership Deed and Managerial Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Notary (Notaire) under the Ministry of Justice civil-law framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the general partner and any subscribing limited partners to execute the partnership deed in one original before a Luxembourg notary. Ensure the deed states the SCSp legal form, duration, registered office, corporate object (digital health software, biometric telemetry analytics, and data processing), allocation of capital, and the powers of the gérant. Where no real property is contributed, the deed may be executed as a private writing, but notarization is recommended to facilitate RCSL registration and third-party banking.
required_dossiers: Certified passports / IDs of partners
Certificate of good standing and corporate documents for a corporate general partner
Signed partnership deed (draft reviewed by Luxembourg counsel)
Registered office address attestation and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the RCSL flags incomplete clauses (e.g., corporate object, capital allocation or management powers), execute an amending addendum to the deed and re-notarize prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCSL Registration and Beneficial Ownership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed and notarized (or validly signed private) partnership deed together with the manager appointment form to the RCSL. Complete the registration module with the SCSp legal form code, NACE/ISIC 6201 activity, registered office, manager details, and stated capital (which may be zero). File the declaration of beneficial owners and the register of limited partners with the RCSL beneficial ownership register (RBE), ensuring full transparency of natural persons holding any controlling interest.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership deed
RCSL new registrations form
Manager appointment form and signed consents
Beneficial ownership declaration (RBE form)
Power of attorney if filing by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any RCSL observations within the statutory 15-day deadline and resubmit the affected module; if registration is suspended, supplement with apostilled or certified translations of foreign partner documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), administered by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the registered deed and the updated company data are published electronically in RESA after RCSL acceptance. Publication in RESA produces legal effects vis-à-vis third parties (opposability). The publication is processed automatically as part of the LBR registration bundle; verify the published excerpt for accuracy in French or German.
required_dossiers: RCSL registration receipt
RESA excerpt text in French or German
Registered address and manager details as filed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the transcript contains material errors, file a rectification request with LBR; where third-party harm is shown, coordinate with the notary on a corrective addendum and re-publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Employer Social Security and Data Protection Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS); National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT on a taxable person basis, given B2C digital app sales through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing (Luxembourg place of supply for domestic consumer downloads; reverse-charge or non-established treatment for non-Luxembourg business customers). Register as an employer with CCSS where staff will be engaged. File the data-processing records and a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) with CNPD for health and fitness biometric telemetry data, and appoint an EU representative if required for non-EU processing controllers.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form (form 1)
RESA / RCSL registration excerpt
Employer registration questionnaire
DPIA and GDPR Art. 30 processing records for CNPD
Identity documents of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT allocates an incorrect VAT regime, file a correction form with the B2C/B2B revenue split and re-submit supporting evidence; CNPD observations are cured by amending the processing records and re-filing the DPIA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit for ISIC 6201 (Autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for Middle Classes (via MyGuichet.lu business platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Launch the electronic application for the establishment authorization covering computer programming, consulting and digital telemetry services. Certify the professional competence and good standing of the manager(s), provide evidence of the registered office and, where relevant, professional indemnity cover. The permit is delivered as a digital decision and recorded in the national business register, authorizing the lawful commencement of the SCSp's app-related commercial activities.
required_dossiers: Establishment permit application form (MyGuichet.lu)
Criminal record extracts (bulletin 3) of the manager(s)
Certificate of good standing for a corporate general partner
Registered office lease and RCSL excerpt
Professional competence declarations for ISIC 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, cure by submitting missing competence evidence or restructuring the manager's mandate and re-apply; an administrative appeal lies to the administrative tribunal within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — General Directorate for Middle Classes; co-supervised by the Ministry of Health for wellness data flows
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement — Information Technology and Software Service Activities (ISIC 6201 / NACE 62.01)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C / Non-classified (exempt) — pure software and telemetry analytics with no physical production facility; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report required; only environmental registration formalities apply when occupying office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No regulated point-source wastewater, VOC, or stack emissions for digital services. Compliance is required with municipal sewer and stormwater bylaws for office wet rooms, the EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for e-waste take-back of IT hardware, and general office waste-segregation obligations. No greenhouse gas or air-discharge site permit is triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) to be obtained from the competent commune for the leased office premises; structural load attestation for any co-located server or equipment rooms; occupational clearance via the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workplace ergonomics, electrical safety, and the mandatory workplace risk assessment (évaluation des risques) under the amended Law of 17 June 1994.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), 33 Rue de Gasperich, L-5826 Hesperange, portal impotsdirects.public.lu (e-filing via eCDF). Indirect taxes and VAT: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), 1-3 Avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg, portal aedt.public.lu (e-filing via eTVA). Company registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the MyGuichet.lu portal. Customs: Administration des douanes et accises (ADdA) via eDouane.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SCSp by notarial deed and file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu; the RCS issues the 13-digit national identification number (matricule/numéro d'identification), which is the tax registration number for direct-tax purposes. 2) Register for VAT by filing Form 640 (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu or eTVA; the AEDT issues the VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits within roughly 2-4 weeks. 3) Non-established foreign suppliers of digital services may alternatively register under the Non-Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) special scheme, and the Union OSS is available for EU-established suppliers to declare cross-border B2C electronic supplies; OSS returns are filed electronically with the AEDT. 4) Obtain an EORI number from the ADdA through eDouane for any customs export/import activity. 5) File VAT returns (monthly/quarterly via eTVA) and the SCSp's annual accounts with the RCS; each partner declares its allocable share of income in its own tax return and non-resident partners file a Luxembourg tax return for any Luxembourg-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope applies at partner level
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default under Article 2(2) LIR (no Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax at entity level). There is no general domestic check-the-box regime; however: (i) US investors may file Form 8832 to elect partnership or association status for US federal tax purposes because the SCSp is not a per se corporation; (ii) a joint option by all partners to subject the SCSp to corporate income tax/municipal business tax/net wealth tax is available for certain Luxembourg partnerships; (iii) ATAD II reverse-hybrid rules (Article 168septies LIR, in force from 1 January 2022) re-characterise the SCSp as a Luxembourg taxable entity where the partner's home jurisdiction treats it as opaque and the mismatch results in double non-taxation; (iv) hybrid-mismatch rules (Articles 168quinquies-168sexies LIR) restrict deductions for hybrid financial instruments and disregarded payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises (VAT Law Art. 57); no registration threshold for non-established foreign taxable persons; EUR 10,000 threshold for intra-Community distance sales and cross-border telecommunications/broadcasting/electronic (TBE) services supplied by an EU-established supplier under the OSS scheme
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no continuous transaction controls, no real-time fiscal clearance, and no digital stamping regime. Electronic invoicing is permitted for B2B provided the invoice guarantees authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility (e.g., EDI, PEPPOL, or qualified electronic signature). B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via the PEPPOL network under the law of 17 July 2020 and EU Directive 2014/55/EU for all Luxembourg public-sector procurement. VAT returns, European Sales Lists and OSS declarations are filed electronically through eTVA; the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' initiative will introduce harmonised e-invoicing and digital reporting for intra-EU supplies once adopted and is not yet in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital health-fitness app (ISIC 6201) - 0%/outside scope applies: (a) B2B supplies of electronic services: place of supply is the customer's establishment (Art. 44 VAT Directive); no Luxembourg VAT is chargeable when the customer is established outside Luxembourg, reverse charge applying for EU customers and outside scope for non-EU customers, evidenced by the customer's valid VAT ID or business registration; (b) B2C supplies directly by the SCSp: place of supply is the consumer's residence (Arts. 58/59 VAT Directive); non-EU consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT scope (effective 0%) and EU consumers trigger Luxembourg VAT unless the Union OSS is used to declare the consumer-country rate; (c) App-store distribution through Apple IAP/Google Play Billing: the marketplace is the deemed supplier (Art. 9a Implementing Regulation 282/2011), so the SCSp's supply to the marketplace operator is an out-of-scope/B2B reverse-charge supply; (d) Physical goods exports: 0% applies where the goods leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch, evidenced by the customs export declaration (SAD/EAD with MRN) and transport documents. Input VAT on related costs remains deductible under the normal rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EAD with MRN) issued by the Administration des douanes et accises
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate and/or bank SWIFT payment statement evidencing receipt of foreign sales proceeds
Commercial invoice and service contract describing the digital/offshore supply
Customer VAT identification number or business registration certificate (for B2B services)
App-store sales reports and marketplace deemed-supplier records for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg applies no foreign-exchange controls or statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline (EU free movement of capital); the 180-day benchmark is used as commercial substantiation practice for the export/offshore service and payment flow. The AEDT may reassess within the standard 5-year VAT limitation period, extended to 10 years where fraud is proven. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating/outside-scope claims are clawed back with (i) the unpaid VAT at 17%, (ii) late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, and (iii) administrative fines up to EUR 12,500. Where intent is established, criminal tax-fraud penalties under Article 181 of the VAT Law of 12 February 1979 range from EUR 125 to EUR 12,500 plus imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years; customs export fraud is additionally sanctioned under the General Customs Law with fines up to twice the evaded duties and confiscation of the goods. Deemed-supplier arrangements with Apple/Google and the apportionment of Luxembourg-source revenue among SCSp partners are specific audit focus points.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and under the prudential supervisory oversight of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area jurisdiction with fully liberalised capital and current account movements under EU law. The euro is freely convertible and there are no residual exchange control restrictions for non-resident investors in a Luxembourg SCSp. Profit distributions and capital redemptions to non-resident partners or unitholders may be made without prior regulatory approval. An SCSp is treated as fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax, and profit distributions are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax. Where a foreign partner is a tax resident in a non-EU jurisdiction, the bank may require additional evidence of economic substance and beneficial ownership to prevent treaty shopping or BEPS-related challenges, but no central bank conversion or inward/outward remittance permit is required. The only non-monetary hurdles are statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the BCL for cross-border flows above certain thresholds, and CSSF/KYC documentation standards applied by Luxembourg banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or holding period applies to Luxembourg digital commerce entities. All export and app-store proceeds, including revenue from Apple, Google Play, and enterprise licensing, may be retained in EUR or in freely convertible foreign currency. For statistical transparency, cross-border payment transactions must be reported to the BCL under the balance-of-payments reporting framework, usually through the settlement bank or on a direct reporting basis if the SCSp transacts above the applicable thresholds. There is no timeline for surrender and no ratio requiring conversion into EUR.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional and Medium for EEA-authorised Electronic Money Institutions or Payment Institutions passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2; Low for offshore or unregulated digital EMIs. An offshore EMI without an EU banking licence or PSD2 passport cannot lawfully provide Luxembourg IBANs, clearing accounts, or regulated payment services. Even a licensed EEA EMI may be used only as a secondary treasury circuit for disbursements, not as the primary capital escrow provider, because EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot accept deposits or deliver full banking escrow services of the kind expected by CSSF for a corporate capital raise. The primary banking relationship for the SCSp should remain with a Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The general partner and all authorised signatories of the SCSp must complete full KYC. In practice, Luxembourg tier-one banks require at least one physical presence of the general partner or ultimate controlling person during initial onboarding, or when opening an escrow account where commercial substance is being evidenced. A purely remote opening is sometimes possible if the bank can perform an equivalent eIDAS-compliant video identification and obtain an advanced qualified electronic signature, but many private and commercial banks still mandate an in-person interview or notarised certification of identity. To minimise onboarding friction, at least one general partner director or professional manager should have an EU/Luxembourg presence and be prepared to attend the bank interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Appearance of an offshore LP or non-EU beneficial owner with no coherent link to the Luxembourg digital health application and biometric data business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial SCSp deed and partnership regulation, signed and updated register of beneficial owners filed with the Luxembourg RBE, group organisational chart, bank and professional references, source of wealth and source of funds evidence, tax residence certificates, and a written business plan demonstrating the commercial rationale for the Luxembourg platform and the investor's role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inflows coming from app-store payout accounts, aggregators, or digital platform accounts rather than from traditional bank transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original Apple Developer and Google Play Console agreements, payout reports, merchant of record agreements, transaction ledger, invoice reconciliation, GDPR and health-data compliance policies, and a clear audit trail demonstrating that app-store collections are linked to sales ledgers and corporate treasury records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency outbound payments to software developers, cloud providers, licensors, or overseas procurement entities under a pass-through SCSp structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service level agreements, development milestone attestations, itemised invoices, vendor KYC file, transfer pricing documentation for the Luxembourg entity, VAT/OSS registration evidence, and bank letters confirming business purpose and expected transaction pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity over who is the true account holder and taxpayer because an SCSp has no legal personality and is fiscally transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal tax and legal opinion confirming the SCSp qualification, the civil-law nature of the Luxembourg special limited partnership, signed delegation of management authority to the general partner, the partnership's Luxembourg RCS registration extract, partner tax status forms, and a statement of allocations demonstrating that Luxembourg income tax burdens are allocated to partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital subscriptions and shareholder loans are routed by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's home bank to the Luxembourg SCSp's designated corporate account. The remittance reference must cite the subscription agreement number and the identity of the SCSp to allow the receiving Luxembourg bank to assign the proper balance-of-payments statistical category for direct investment or capital transfers to the BCL. For any non-EUR injection, the bank will require the underlying subscription in EUR or an executed FX conversion contract. The supporting documents must include the executed subscription agreement, call notice, source of funds evidence, beneficial ownership confirmation, and, where applicable, the Luxembourg partnership deed. Compliance with EU sanctions and anti-money-laundering checks is completed before value is credited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outbound payments to EEA suppliers are executed through SEPA Credit Transfers using ISO 20022 XML with the SCSp's legal name and purpose reference. Payments outside the EEA are executed through SWIFT MT103 with a valid UETR and structured remittance data. High-value physical or licensing-based trade transactions may be backed by a Commercial Letter of Credit, although for a digital health app the primary clearing rails are MT103 and SEPA. The bank will apply collective mandate limits, dual-approval controls, and monthly BCL balance-of-payments reporting. Vendor payments over agreed thresholds require supporting invoices, contracts, and sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Permissible forwards: EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other freely convertible currency outright forwards with a licensed Luxembourg or EU bank counterparty
NDFs: non-deliverable forwards permitted for emerging-market currencies only where a demonstrable underlying revenue or procurement exposure exists and the bank accepts the credit and regulatory risk

Currency swaps: FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps used to hedge multi-currency cash positions, long-term subscription capital, and cross-border development expenditure in currencies outside the euro area

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial owner validation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary date of the initial RBE registration, and at least once each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines ranging from EUR 125 to EUR 5,000; defaulting entities may be prohibited from making payments to partners; general partner exposed to personal and criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SCSp annual partnership tax return including corporate income tax declaration for transparent entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the tax year; electronic extension to 31 December is available upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to 10% of assessed tax, default tax assessment by the administration, late-payment interest, and suspension of tax clearance certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg VAT return and, where applicable, EU OSS digital services declaration for B2C fitness app subscriptions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual Luxembourg VAT return due by 30 April of the following calendar year; OSS quarterly declarations due by the last day of the month following each calendar quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; criminal fines for failure to file; administrative enforcement and VAT reassessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (only where size or legal trigger applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within 6 months of financial year-end and filed with the RCS within one month after approval; in all cases not later than 7 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 5,000, court-ordered filing, inability to rely on accounts in legal proceedings, and risk of judicial liquidation for persistent default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) where the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also required for public-interest entities, regulated financial undertakings, and where unlimited-liability general partners are themselves companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2020 implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts and may be voluntarily adopted for the SCSp's individual accounts by decision of the general partner.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain the beneficial ownership file and submit the annual RBE confirmation within one month of the RBE registration anniversary. Any transfer of limited partner interests or other change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change. Beneficial owners include any natural person ultimately owning or controlling more than 10% of the partnership through capital participation or other means of control.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable until audit thresholds are triggered; when triggered, USD 5,500 – USD 16,500 (EUR 5,000 – EUR 15,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level (fiscally transparent partnership, not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax). A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner is exposed to the aggregate Luxembourg corporate tax burden of 24.94% in Luxembourg City, composed of 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and a 6.75% municipal business tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP-box exemption on net qualifying software and copyright income (approximate aggregate effective rate 4.99%); 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; no notional interest deduction material at current low yields; investment tax credits may be available for eligible digital capital expenditure; losses carried forward indefinitely but cannot be carried back.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory cap (indefinite carryforward; no carryback permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 451 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu pour les collectivités) covering corporate income tax and municipal business tax, filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / ACD (Administration des contributions directes) e-filing portal. Form 470 is additionally used for net wealth tax where a taxable partner has a permanent establishment in Luxembourg. A fully tax-transparent SCSp typically files a nil return or an informational return only upon request by the ACD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year (usually 30 June for a 31 December year-end); in practice, the ACD routinely and automatically extends the electronic filing deadline to 31 December of the following calendar year for returns filed via MyGuichet.lu by, or on behalf of, a registered professional tax adviser.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg NIF, registered office address, legal form (SCSp), fiscal year-end, and the name and address of the Luxembourg-resident manager (gérant).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp has no Luxembourg corporate partner and is not registered for corporate income tax, the return is informational only; the Luxembourg contact person must be identified for service of process and tax correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section II – Partnership status and partner allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of fiscal transparency, list of partners, country of tax residence, tax identification number of each partner, partnership ratio, profit-sharing ratio, and effective date of changes in partnership holdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp manager must provide each non-resident partner with a statement of allocable profit/loss for foreign tax purposes; no Luxembourg tax is withheld at the SCSp level on allocations to partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit derived from the health fitness app, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing gross revenue, platform commissions, refunds, merchant fees, cloud hosting, engineering wages, licensing costs, and amortisation of developed software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident partner has no Luxembourg permanent establishment, the app's mobile platform revenues should not be reported by the SCSp as attributable Luxembourg taxable income; the partner reports its allocation in its residence jurisdiction under applicable DTA and local rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All deductible operating expenses, arm's-length management fees, amortisation and depreciation, R&D payroll, marketing costs, and any deductible app acquisition costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure invoices received from related parties satisfy Luxembourg documentation rules and that cross-border payments are at arm's length; substantiation must be retained in Luxembourg or be available to the ACD on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 80% exemption on net income from qualifying intellectual property (copyrighted software code, patents) under the Luxembourg IP regime, subject to the nexus formula requiring eligible R&D expenditures and documentation of IP ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IP must be legally documented in Luxembourg, the taxpayer must evidence economic ownership and active management of the IP, and the non-resident partner claiming the benefit must register a Luxembourg tax filing and meet substance conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses carried forward and utilised against taxable profit in the current year; Luxembourg permits an indefinite carryforwards but requires continuity of ownership and no anti-abuse disqualification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident partner may not claim Luxembourg loss carryforward against its home-country income unless it is taxable in Luxembourg through a permanent establishment and the losses are attributable to that permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the gérant, tax adviser (if any), date, place of signature, and acknowledgement of civil and criminal liability for inaccurate declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident manager may not sign the Luxembourg declaration if the gérant is not tax-resident in Luxembourg; a Luxembourg-resident authorised agent is required for valid fiscal representation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and failure to file may trigger an administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000; 0.6% per month late-payment interest on any assessed tax; an automatic estimated assessment (taxation d'office) that shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer; and criminal fines for fraudulent filing or persistent non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions made by the SCSp itself because a fiscally transparent SCSp is not a Luxembourg resident company and does not make statutory dividend withholdable distributions. Where the SCSp, or a partner, receives dividends from an underlying Luxembourg resident company, the domestic Luxembourg withholding tax rate is 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent–Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying 10% participation held for 12 months, and generally reduced to 5%–15% under most double tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief on upstream Luxembourg dividends, the beneficial owner must submit the official ACD exemption request, attaching an original or apostilled tax residence certificate issued by the partner's fiscal authority, a declaration of beneficial ownership, and evidence of the shareholding period. The application is made electronically via MyGuichet.lu before the distribution; if withholding has been applied, a refund claim must be filed within the statutory limitation period. For SCSp distributions to non-resident partners, no such reclaim is required because no withholding tax is levied at the partnership level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on outgoing royalties or ordinary arm's-length interest payments to non-residents. Treaty rates are typically 0% for royalties and 0%–10% for interest, and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive provides a 0% rate for qualifying associated companies. Certain payments may be recharacterised as constructive dividends where a loan is profit-participating or paid by an entity with inadequate equity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers the requirement to prepare and maintain Luxembourg Master File and Local File documentation; EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers the Country-by-Country Report threshold. In audit practice, the ACD may require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation even below the EUR 50 million threshold where material related-party transactions exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulations similar to the UAE, but it applies a substantive business-purpose doctrine, the statutory general anti-abuse rule (LIR §168bis), ATAD anti-hybrid rules, and extensive case law requiring genuine local substance to access treaty benefits and tax transparency. An SCSp engaged in a digital health app business should maintain a Luxembourg registered office, a Luxembourg-resident manager, local bank accounts, local books and records, minutes of partner and manager decisions, and actual strategic control over pricing, marketing, and intellectual property to withstand an ACD substance challenge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate income tax declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Apple IAP or Google Play Billing subscription revenue, fabricating platform settlement statements, inflating deductible royalties to a related zero-tax entity, or concealing the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to five years; the taxpayer is required to pay all taxes due plus a punitive surcharge and statutory interest at 0.6% per month; the ACD may reopen previously closed assessments and impose penalties equal to a substantial percentage of the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and controlling directors may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes in cases of fraud or gross mismanagement; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment, confiscation of assets, and travel bans imposed during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file annual Luxembourg tax return or nil return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not filing Form 451 for the SCSp or a Luxembourg corporate partner by the statutory deadline, ignoring an ACD request for a nil return, or failing to file a partner-level Luxembourg return where an SCSp has been used to carry on an active app business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on any assessed amount; discretionary assessment by the ACD with reversal of the burden of proof, leading to estimated high profits and denial of otherwise deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who have knowingly failed to file may be personally assessed for fines and interest; in serious cases, the failure to file after a formal demand may be treated as tax evasion and expose directors to criminal sanctions and civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties for the health app's software code to a related intellectual property company without economic substance, without a written licence agreement, without a valuation of the intangible, or without evidence of active development risks transferred.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD will apply the arm's-length principle under LIR §164 and disallow the excessive deduction, computing additional taxable income in the SCSp or Luxembourg partner at the 24.94% aggregate corporate rate; a 10% tax penalty and 0.6% per month late interest will be added; serious cases are referred to the criminal tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp manager who approved the intercompany royalty may be held personally liable for the additional corporate tax if the arrangement was not properly documented or if they acted in bad faith; professional service providers may be subject to civil liability for assisting in abusive arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of SCSp transparency and shell company arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating and maintaining the SCSp purely as a Luxembourg mailbox with no staff, no local bank account, no local management decisions, no office or business function, while the entire mobile health app business is controlled and performed abroad, solely to exploit Luxembourg partnership pass-through treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may disregard the SCSp for tax purposes and treat a non-resident partner as having a Luxembourg permanent establishment, applying Luxembourg corporate income tax at 24.94% plus solidarity and municipal business tax; the entity may be denied all treaty benefits; administrative fines and penalties up to EUR 25,000 may be imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may be jointly liable for taxes assessed upon recharacterisation; criminal sanctions up to five years' imprisonment may apply where the shell arrangement is used to conceal the true economic beneficiary or to launder funds, and a travel ban may be imposed pending proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CTF violation through misuse of app payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the health fitness app's Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant accounts as an unregistered payment collection vehicle, intentionally commingling subscription revenue with proceeds from third parties, or processing transactions designed to circumvent know-your-customer controls and anti-money-laundering obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg anti-money-laundering law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) criminalises money laundering with imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 1,250,000; illicit proceeds and instrumentalities are subject to confiscation; administrative AML fines may be imposed in parallel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly participate in or tolerate such schemes are personally criminally liable and may face imprisonment, confiscation of personal assets, director disqualification, and travel restrictions designed to secure the enforcement of monetary penalties.
